\chapter{Iteration 1: Design and Implementation}
\section{Iteration Objectives}\label{ch6:sec:objectives}
The objective of Iteration 1, fixed in \path{docs/08-MidEval/iteration-plan.md} before the work began, was: on a seeded fixture and with no application logs, FlakeTrace shows the victim passing alone and failing after its polluter, minimises the order, names the shared resource from bytecode, reproduces the failure $n$ times with a confidence interval, and verifies that the source is unchanged; a negative control must be reported \texttt{UNRESOLVED}.

The work was split into fourteen work packages. Member 3 built the fixture, statistics, outcome decision and baselines (W1--W4); Member 1 built the static extractor (W8); Member 2 built the repository and CI, the order runner, the diagnosis runs, minimisation and the order search (W5--W7, W10, W14); Members 2 and 3 joined the parts into one command (W9); the report, the tag and the rehearsed demo are shared (W11--W13).

\section{Selected Use Cases / Features}\label{ch6:sec:features}
The use cases marked \guillemotleft iteration 1\guillemotright{} in Figure~\ref{ch4:fig:usecases} (UC1--UC7) form one flow: a developer diagnoses one failing test with one command and receives a report. The flow is exercised on seven cases in the seeded Maven project \path{fixtures/od-fixture}, whose expected outcomes Member 3 wrote in \path{ground_truth.json} before any run:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Normal cases.} F1: a polluter sets the static field \texttt{Config.mode} and never restores it. F2: a polluter sets the system property \texttt{odfixture.turbo}, which the victim reads one call below the test method.
  \item \textbf{Edge cases.} F3: the victim fails only when \emph{both} \texttt{setFlagA} and \texttt{setFlagB} run before it, so no single test is the polluter. F4: the polluter's class sorts after the victim's, so the discovered order never fails and another order has to be found.
  \item \textbf{Negative controls.} N1 fails alone every time; N2 fails at random, independent of order; N3 models a failure that depends on the environment and never reproduces locally. FlakeTrace must blame no test in any of them.
\end{itemize}
Each case maps to a step of the live demonstration (Section~\ref{ch6:sec:demo}).

\section{Design}\label{ch6:sec:design}
The design is described in Chapter~5: the components and their contracts in Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:arch}, one \texttt{diagnose} run in Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:diagnose-seq}, and the reproduce--search--minimise--verify logic in Figure~\ref{ch5:fig:search-activity}. This chapter describes how that design is implemented and how to run it.

\subsection{Setup and running}
FlakeTrace needs Python 3.11 or newer, a JDK 8 or newer (\texttt{java}, \texttt{javac}, \texttt{javap}) and Maven on \texttt{PATH}. The commands below are copied from the root \path{README.md} and are run from the repository root; this is the Windows form (the README also gives the same steps for Linux and macOS):
\begin{lstlisting}[basicstyle=\footnotesize\ttfamily,breaklines=true,breakatwhitespace=true,columns=fullflexible,caption={Setup and checks (Windows), from \texttt{README.md}},label=ch6:lst:setup]
py -m pip install -r eval/requirements.txt
py -m unittest -v eval.tests.test_baseline eval.tests.test_examples eval.tests.test_outcome eval.tests.test_report eval.tests.test_schema_validator eval.tests.test_stats eval.tests.test_yield_report
mvn -B -f fixtures/od-fixture/pom.xml test-compile
py -m unittest -v runner.tests.test_cli runner.tests.test_diagnose runner.tests.test_discovery runner.tests.test_integrity runner.tests.test_minimise runner.tests.test_order_runner runner.tests.test_orders runner.tests.test_recording runner.tests.test_search
py -m runner diagnose --project fixtures/od-fixture --victim odfixture.ConfigVictimTest#expectsDefaultMode
mvn -B -q -f evidence/tests/resources/m1-selftest/pom.xml test-compile
py -m unittest -v evidence.tests.test_extract
\end{lstlisting}

Before quoting them here, Member 2 ran every one of these commands on 11 October 2026 on Windows 11 with Python 3.14.0, JDK 21.0.9 and Maven 3.10.0 (\path{docs/evidence-m2.md}, entry ``Root README''). Table~\ref{ch6:tab:setup-results} gives the results. The same test suites run in CI on every pull request, on Linux with JDK 8 and Python 3.11.

The \texttt{diagnose} command writes one execution record (\texttt{.jsonl}, one line per JVM run) and one report (\texttt{.report.json}) to \path{flaketrace-records/}, which git ignores.
